title: 2026-12-28 POC scoping: hosted vs dedicated vs private - Aurora Payments
summary: Initial POC scoping between Redwood and Aurora Payments to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and deployment decision criteria (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Action items: share pricing worksheet, security pack, benchmark plan; Aurora to share traffic traces and confirm infra constraints. Tentative POC: 2 weeks for hosted baseline + dedicated/private evaluation if needed.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private decision criteria
next_steps: Alex - send pricing worksheet + hosted vs dedicated config doc (link)
Jamie - send benchmark plan and sample load script
Maya - share 7 days of production traces and token distribution
Samira - receive SOC2/ISO whitepaper and encryption details
action_items: Alex: email pricing worksheet and dedicated capacity options - due 2027-01-04
Jamie: draft benchmark plan (replay + synthetic) and test harness - due 2026-12-31
Maya: export and share 7 days of traces + sample payloads - due 2026-12-30
Ethan: confirm VPC peering, firewall rules, and egress constraints - due 2027-01-06
Samira: provide security contact and list of compliance questions - due 2027-01-03
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-12-28 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Jamie (Redwood SE), Taylor (CSM); Raj, Maya, Ethan, Leslie, Samira (Aurora)
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick intros?
[00:08] Raj: Raj here, CTO at Aurora Payments, we run payments infra and want to add LLM features for dispute resolution and routing, hey all.
[00:16] Maya: Maya, head of ML. We're evaluating inference options, curious about latency/cost and security tradeoffs.
[00:23] Ethan: Ethan, infra, I'll be looking at networking and VPC peering constraints.
[00:27] Alex: Awesome, great. Jamie from Redwood will cover the technical scoping and benchmarking plan. Jamie, over to you.

[00:33] Jamie: Cool thanks. Quick agenda: agree success criteria, measure current workload sizing, propose benchmark approach (replay vs synthetic), and discuss timelines and deployment decision factors for hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:44] Leslie: Sounds good. Our initial ask is to understand what the POC will prove and how we decide between hosted/dedicated/private after the POC.

[00:51] Jamie: Totally. On success criteria, we typically see customers set: p95 latency targets, throughput/reqs-per-second, cost per token or per-call budget, and correctness sensitivity (response quality). What are Aurora's targets?

[01:05] Maya: For the dispute assistant: p95 end-to-end latency target is under 350ms for short prompts (~200 tokens). Throughput target is about 80 concurrent requests during peak. Cost target is roughly 15% of current per-interaction compute budget, but flexible.
[01:22] Alex: Good—so p95 <350ms, 80 concurrency. We should capture average tokens per request and distribution; that affects batching and kernel choices. Do you have token histogram?
[01:32] Maya: We'll share traces. Most requests are short 30-150 tokens, some longer ones up to 800 when generating explanation drafts.

[01:41] Jamie: Perfect. For benchmarks we propose two phases: 1) hosted baseline: run replayed traffic against Redwood hosted API to measure p50/p95 and costs; 2) if you need predictability/SLA or VPC, we scope a dedicated cluster or private deployment and run the replay there. Hosted can often prove viability in 1 week, dedicated/private setup adds provisioning time.
[01:58] Raj: Provisioning time numbers would be helpful. What are realistic lead times for dedicated and private?

[02:05] Jamie: Dedicated: typically 2-4 weeks to provision reserved capacity depending on GPU types and region; Private (VPC or on-prem) tends to be 4-8 weeks because of networking, KMS integration, and any air-gapped requirements. We'll include that in the timeline doc.
[02:20] Samira: From a security POV, our requirements: SOC2, encryption at rest with customer KMS, audit logs, and SSO via SAML. Are those supported out of the box?

[02:30] Alex: Yes—Redwood supports SOC2 controls, KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated (hosted can use managed keys), SAML SSO and audit logs. We'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary).
[02:40] Samira: Great. Also need data residency options—some data must not leave EU for a subset of customers.

[02:47] Jamie: For data residency, Private or region-restricted Dedicated nodes are recommended; hosted can be region-backed but if you need strict isolation, Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is the usual path.
[02:58] Ethan: About networking, we need to confirm whether Redwood supports VPC peering vs private link; also firewall egress rules are important.

[03:06] Jamie: We support both VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on cloud. We'll capture specifics per your cloud account. For egress, we can limit outbound to specific IPs and provide FQDNs for endpoints.
[03:15] Leslie: Back to benchmarks—what metrics will you collect besides latency and throughput? Token consumption, cost, fallback rates, and model quality?

[03:22] Jamie: Yes. We'll collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per response, throughput, token cost estimates, and basic quality checks (sample prompts + human eval or automated similarity scores). We'll also run warm vs cold cache tests to show KV cache benefits.
[03:35] Maya: For quality gates, we need to measure hallucination rate on a holdout set and trigger regression alerts if model changes increase error by X%.
[03:42] Alex: We can integrate Redwood Optimize to track evals and regressions; for POC we'll run an eval harness using your prompt set and give a baseline score.
[03:50] Raj: Cost talk—can you ballpark hosted per token costs and how dedicated changes the economics?

[03:56] Alex: Hosted for the models you might use tends to be higher per-token but zero infra ops; dedicated reduces unit cost by ~30-60% depending on utilization and quantization. We will provide example numbers in the pricing worksheet. For very high throughput private, quantized models on dedicated hardware are best.
[04:12] Ethan: We will likely test both hosted and a small dedicated pool; can we run side-by-side benchmarks?
[04:17] Jamie: Yes, that's the plan—hosted baseline first (fast to set up), then dedicated. Private we only recommend if you have strict compliance or data residency needs.
[04:25] Leslie: Timeline suggestion from Aurora: we want baseline hosted benchmarks within 2 weeks and a decision by mid-January. Is that feasible?

[04:31] Jamie: Feasible. Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) - exchange traces and access; Week 1 - Redwood runs hosted replay and shares report; Week 2 - if needed, set up dedicated POC and run dedicated benchmarks (can be parallel if you provision accounts quickly). Decision meeting in week 3.
[04:45] Raj: Dependencies? What do you need from us upfront?

[04:48] Jamie: 1) 7 days of production traces with request/response sizes and timestamps, 2) sample payloads for quality evals, 3) your list of allowed IPs/cloud region preference, 4) compliance questions. We'll provide a template and sample load script.
[05:02] Maya: We'll produce traces and mask PII, should be able to get that by Wednesday.

[05:07] Alex: Great — we'll also provision a hosted test API key and a sandbox dataset; you'll get links to the benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/aurora-123 and security pack: https://redwood.app/security/soc2.pdf
[05:18] Samira: On KMS — for dedicated/private, can we bring our own key material (HSM)?
[05:22] Jamie: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we'll document key rotation and audit log flow.
[05:30] Raj: Any blockers you foresee?

[05:33] Jamie: Mostly timing around dedicated hardware and network approvals; nothing technical that we've seen that would prevent a POC. If you try hosted first we can typically show if we meet latency/cost goals quickly.
[05:42] Ethan: For the dedicated cluster sizing, what inputs do you need to estimate GPUs and pods?

[05:47] Jamie: We need: qps during peak, average tokens per request, typical sequence lengths, and acceptable p95 latency. With that we model batching and GPU types (e.g., A100 vs H100 or cost-optimised 8-bit quantized variants).
[05:59] Maya: To be concrete: peak qps 80, avg tokens 120, p95 <350ms. If you could sketch a couple of hardware options we can compare costs vs hosted.
[06:08] Alex: We'll include two sizing options: cost-optimized (quantized) and performance-optimized (larger GPU). We'll also show autoscaling behavior and burst capacity options.
[06:17] Leslie: What about model variants — do you recommend using a smaller model for latency-critical paths and a larger one for depth?

[06:23] Jamie: Yes — routing by policy is a common approach: quick, smaller model for short prompts; bigger model for longer context or high-quality outputs. Redwood supports automatic fallback and routing policies.
[06:32] Raj: Decision criteria recap — when would we pick Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?

[06:36] Alex: High-level: Hosted if you want fastest time-to-value and lower ops; Dedicated if you need predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale, and some degree of isolation; Private if you require full network isolation, strict regulatory controls, or on-prem needs. We'll put a decision matrix in the doc.
[06:49] Samira: Also consider auditability and KMS — Private gives most control, Dedicated supports customer KMS, hosted uses managed keys unless you opt for bring-your-own in some regions.
[06:58] Jamie: We'll also run a cold-start vs warm cache comparison because KV cache can change latency profiles a lot. We'll show cached p95 vs uncached p95.
[07:06] Maya: For quality gating, we want automated regression alerts tied to eval sets; is that part of Redwood Optimize?
[07:12] Alex: Yes, Redwood Optimize does eval tracking, regression alerts, and suggests quantization profiles by workload.
[07:18] Raj: Anything else we should plan for?

[07:21] Jamie: We'll do a short checklist: data ingestion and masking, traffic replay script, a small set of evaluation prompts, target metrics and thresholds, network contacts for peering, and your security questionnaire. Once we have those we can kick off the hosted run.
[07:34] Leslie: Ok going to confirm internal stakeholders and timeline, looks good.

[07:37] Alex: Recap and next steps: I'll send pricing worksheet, hosted config guide, security pack and the benchmark template. Jamie will share the load script and test harness. Maya will send traces by Wednesday. We'll aim for a hosted baseline run next week and follow-up decision meeting the week after.
[07:54] Maya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:56] Raj: Thanks, appreciate the clear plan.
[07:58] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links and action items. Back channel: CRM-AUR-12458 for reference. Bye.
[08:03] (call ends)
Notes on transcription: some words may be slightly off; proper nouns might be mis-transcribed (Kubernetes/Koo-ber-ne-tees, KV cache sometimes 'KV cash').
